title: Semilinear naturality and coherence of normalized free realizations
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For every commutative ring sheaf $B$ and set sheaf $E$ on either site write $B[E]$ for the module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of $U\mapsto B(U)[E(U)]$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], with restrictions $\sum b_e[e]\mapsto\sum(b_e|_V)[e|_V]$ and generator $i_{B,E}$. Let $L:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ preserve finite limits, transporting ring and module operations by the finite-product comparisons [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose for each $B,E$ that restriction along $Li_{B,E}$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{LB}(L(B[E]),H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(LE,|H|)$ for every $LB$-module sheaf $H$. Suppose given linear isomorphisms $p^L_{B,E}:L(B[E])\cong(LB)[LE]$ with $|p^L_{B,E}|\circ Li_{B,E}=i_{LB,LE}$. For a ring-sheaf map $b:B\to B'$ and set-sheaf map $u:E\to E'$, let $c(b,u):B[E]\to B'[E']$ be the sheafified $b$-semilinear extension $[e]\mapsto[u(e)]$, where semilinear means additive and $c(ax)=b(a)c(x)$. Then, as semilinear maps, $$p^L_{B',E'}\circ Lc(b,u)=c(Lb,Lu)\circ p^L_{B,E}.$$ For any set-sheaf map $v:LE\to F$ on $\mathcal D$, $$|c(1,v)\circ p^L_{B,E}|\circ Li_{B,E}=i_{LB,F}\circ v.$$ In particular, when $E=\prod_{i\in I}E_i$ with $I$ finite and $v$ is the product comparison $\lambda:L(\prod_iE_i)\cong\prod_iLE_i$, this equation holds including $I=\varnothing$, and the squares for the product projections commute. For $L=\mathrm{id}$, $p^L_{B,E}=\mathrm{id}$. If $\mathcal H$ is another small site and $K:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal H)$ preserves finite limits, suppose the same representing property and normalized comparisons are given for $K$ and $KL$, using composite transported operations and underlying-sheaf identifications. Then $$p^{KL}_{B,E}=p^K_{LB,LE}\circ K(p^L_{B,E}).$$ These conclusions require no adjoint to $L$ or $K$ in addition to the stated representing properties.

proof.text: First make the semilinear extension precise. For a ring-sheaf map $b:B\to B'$ and a $B'$-module sheaf $N$, keep its underlying abelian sheaf and define a $B$-action by $a\cdot x=b(a)x$. Its module axioms follow from $b(aa')=b(a)b(a')$, $b(a+a')=b(a)+b(a')$ and $b(1)=1$; its restrictions satisfy $(b(a)x)|_V=b(a|_V)(x|_V)$. Thus it is a $B$-module sheaf, denoted $N_b$, and $B$-linear maps to $N_b$ are exactly $b$-semilinear maps to $N$. Apply the free-sheaf universal property to $N=B'[E']$ and $i_{B',E'}\circ u:E\to|N_b|$. Its unique extension is $c(b,u)$, with $$|c(b,u)|\circ i_{B,E}=i_{B',E'}\circ u.$$ On a finite formal sum its value is $\sum a_e[e]\mapsto\sum b(a_e)[u(e)]$. This formula commutes with restrictions since $b$ and $u$ are sheaf maps; the module-sheafification factorization identifies it with the extension specified in the statement. The same argument applies on each of the three sites in the statement.

proof.text: Check the type of $Lc(b,u)$ before comparing it with other maps. For a $b$-semilinear map $h:M\to N$, write its scalar compatibility as the equality of sheaf maps $h\circ\mu_M=\mu_N\circ(b\times h):B\times|M|\to|N|$, and likewise write additivity and zero compatibility. Apply $L$ to these equalities. The natural finite-product comparison identifies $L(b\times h)$ with $Lb\times Lh$ and identifies the two transported actions with $L\mu_M$ and $L\mu_N$. Consequently $Lh$ is $Lb$-semilinear; additivity and zero follow in exactly the same way from their displayed operation diagrams. This uses only the specified transport of operations. The argument also applies to $K$, in particular to the linear map $p^L_{B,E}$.

source.place: Tag 08TQ (lemma-pullback-differentials), proof, free-module identifications; Tag 04BL (lemma-universal-module), proof, generator extension. Conditional comparison calculus supplied by the worker.

proof.text: Put $P=L(B[E])$ and $N=(LB')[LE']$. The two maps $$A=p^L_{B',E'}\circ Lc(b,u),\qquad D=c(Lb,Lu)\circ p^L_{B,E}$$ are $Lb$-semilinear by step 2 and hence linear maps from $P$ to $N_{Lb}$, the scalar restriction explicitly defined in step 1. Compute their restrictions along $Li_{B,E}$. Functoriality, step 1 and normalization give $$|A|\circ Li_{B,E}=|p^L_{B',E'}|\circ L(i_{B',E'}\circ u)=i_{LB',LE'}\circ Lu,$$ whereas $$|D|\circ Li_{B,E}=|c(Lb,Lu)|\circ i_{LB,LE}=i_{LB',LE'}\circ Lu.$$ The representing bijection assumed for $L,B,E$, applied to the $LB$-module $N_{Lb}$, is injective, so $A=D$. This proves simultaneous naturality, without requiring $b$ to be invertible.

proof.text: For an arbitrary $v:LE\to F$, step 1 on $\mathcal D$ and normalization immediately give $$|c(1,v)\circ p^L_{B,E}|\circ Li_{B,E}=|c(1,v)|\circ i_{LB,LE}=i_{LB,F}\circ v.$$ No assumption that $v$ is an isomorphism is used.

source.place: Tag 08TQ (lemma-pullback-differentials), proof, free-module identifications; Tag 04BL (lemma-universal-module), proof, generator extension. Conditional comparison calculus supplied by the worker.

proof.text: For $E=\prod_i E_i$, set $T=\prod_i LE_i$ and $t=c(1,\lambda)\circ p^L_{B,E}$. Step 4 gives $|t|Li_{B,E}=i_{LB,T}\lambda$. For each projection $\pi_i:E\to E_i$ and $q_i:T\to LE_i$, the definition of the product comparison gives $q_i\lambda=L\pi_i$. The two linear maps $$c(1,q_i)\circ t,\qquad p^L_{B,E_i}\circ Lc(1,\pi_i):L(B[E])\longrightarrow(LB)[LE_i]$$ both restrict along $Li_{B,E}$ to $i_{LB,LE_i}L\pi_i$, by steps 1 and 4 and normalization. Injectivity of the assumed representing bijection proves equality, which is the required projection square. If the index set is empty, $E$ and $T$ are terminal sheaves and $\lambda:L1\cong1$ exists by finite-limit preservation. Step 4 still gives the generator equation; there are no projection squares to check. This case does not identify $B[1]$ with the zero module.

source.place: Tag 08TQ (lemma-pullback-differentials), proof, free-module identifications; Tag 04BL (lemma-universal-module), proof, generator extension. Conditional comparison calculus supplied by the worker.

proof.text: For $L=\mathrm{id}$, the underlying source and target are both $B[E]$ with their original operations. Normalization says $|p^{\mathrm{id}}_{B,E}|i_{B,E}=i_{B,E}=|\mathrm{id}_{B[E]}|i_{B,E}$. The injective restriction-to-generators map of the free-sheaf universal property therefore gives $p^{\mathrm{id}}_{B,E}=\mathrm{id}_{B[E]}$.

source.place: Tag 08TQ (lemma-pullback-differentials), proof, free-module identifications; Tag 04BL (lemma-universal-module), proof, generator extension. Conditional comparison calculus supplied by the worker.

proof.text: For composable $L,K$, work throughout with the composite transported operations and underlying-sheaf identifications required in the statement. Step 2 implies that $$r=p^K_{LB,LE}\circ K(p^L_{B,E}):KL(B[E])\longrightarrow(KLB)[KLE]$$ is $KLB$-linear. Functoriality and the two normalizations compute its restriction as $$|r|\circ KLi_{B,E}=|p^K_{LB,LE}|\circ K(|p^L_{B,E}|\circ Li_{B,E})=|p^K_{LB,LE}|\circ Ki_{LB,LE}=i_{KLB,KLE}.$$ This is also the restriction of $p^{KL}_{B,E}$. Injectivity of the representing bijection assumed for $KL,B,E$ gives $r=p^{KL}_{B,E}$. Every equality used only finite-product transport, the given representing bijections, and normalization; no adjunction for $L$ or $K$ was introduced.
